entries.topicDescription: Structuring a multi-module Android project: module boundaries, dependencies, and build performance.

tips.title: Modularization speeds up builds by letting Gradle skip unaffected modules
tips.content:
In a single-module app, any code change forces Gradle to recompile the
entire codebase, since there's no smaller unit of compilation to isolate
the change to.

Splitting the app into well-bounded modules lets Gradle's incremental
build and build cache skip recompiling modules whose inputs
haven't changed — a change confined to a `:feature:profile` module
doesn't force a rebuild of `:feature:checkout` or `:core:network`,
significantly speeding up iterative local builds on a large codebase.

tips.title: Use implementation, not api, unless a dependency is part of your public API
tips.content:
With implementation, a module's dependencies stay hidden from the modules that depend on it. A change inside the library then only forces recompilation of that library, not of everything above it. api exposes the dependency transitively, so consumers see it on their compile classpath and are rebuilt when it changes.

Use api only when the dependency's types appear in your module's public signatures (parameters, return types, supertypes). Defaulting to implementation keeps module boundaries honest and builds faster.

tips.title: Feature modules should not depend on each other
tips.content:
If :feature:cart depends on :feature:profile and later the reverse is needed, you get a cycle, and every change in one feature rebuilds the other. Keep features independent: each depends only on lower-level modules (:core:ui, :core:data, :core:model), and the :app module wires the features together.

For navigation between features, expose route definitions (or a small navigation interface) from a shared module, or let :app pass navigation callbacks into each feature's entry point.

tips.title: Keep small, stable core modules that features depend on
tips.content:
Split shared code by responsibility, not by size: a :core:model module for plain data types, :core:data for repositories, :core:network and :core:database for the technical details, and :core:ui for shared design-system components. Feature modules then depend only on the parts they need.

The more a module is depended on, the more stable its API should be, because every change forces its dependents to rebuild. Keep the widely shared modules thin and move volatile code into feature modules.
